Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Canary allocator contention — immediate update and mitigation

Jordan / Atlas team,

Thanks again for the quick signal on the spike you saw this morning. I want to summarize what we know so far and the immediate actions we've taken to restore steady serving for your Dedicated cluster in us-west-2 (Canary pool).

Summary (short):
- What happened: sudden allocator contention in the Canary GPU pool caused a subset of your reserved nodes to stall while serving warmup workloads, producing 502/timeout errors for ~8 minutes starting at 08:55 PT.
- Immediate mitigation: we routed active traffic to a compatible model-variant in a warm fallback pool and rolled a hotfix to the autoscaler sidecar to avoid the stale-warmup loop.
- Current state: traffic is stable on the fallback variant; error rates have returned to baseline. We're continuing post-incident validation.

Ask from you: please confirm whether you saw any downstream application retries or duplicated user events tied to 08:50–09:05 PT so we can correlate.

Attachments: brief evidence dump prepared for your ops team (allocator-debug-0310.log; small). We will follow up with a formal postmortem draft and an itemized credit proposal.

Next steps (internal & customer-facing):
- Today: handoff to ops-led postmortem (Ben / Kimberly) and complete evidence packet.
- By Tue 15 Mar: deliver postmortem draft + remediation plan, propose credits and SLA bridge for that window.
- Optional: schedule a 30-min sync to walk through the packet.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts real users and we appreciate your patience. I’m on this thread and available on call if needed.

Cheers,

--
Priyom Das

Subject: RE: Canary allocator contention — immediate update and mitigation (internal)

Folks — quick internal notes while I finish the timeline:

Root cause (short):
- The Canary allocator entered a contention state when the warmup controller retried several long-running KV cache priming calls while a recent roll had left the sidecar rate-limiter at a saturated token count. That combination produced blocked allocator threads and delayed GRPC responses.

Mitigations applied:
1) Emergency traffic reroute to fallback variant (done at 08:56 PT).
2) Autoscaler sidecar patch (prevent duplicate warmup retries) deployed to Canary nodes at 09:04 PT.
3) Increased soft concurrency thresholds for Canary reserved nodes to reduce sensitivity during warmup bursts (09:10 PT).

Planned follow-ups for Atlas packet:
- Full timeline (per-node timestamps)
- Relevant logs (allocator & sidecar traces)
- Proposed config changes to avoid recurrence (patch already staged for Dedicated clusters)
- Credit proposal: pro-rated credit for the 8-minute window + SLA bridge offer for March.

I will compile the evidence and put the postmortem draft into the shared drive. Priyom, can you confirm the customer call time? Jordan asked for 15 Mar 10:00 PT.

Ben
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: Postmortem draft and evidence packet (Canary allocator contention)

Jordan — attaching the postmortem draft and a consolidated evidence packet for your ops and compliance teams. This packet contains:
- per-node timeline with UTC timestamps (allocator-debug-0310.log)
- sidecar trace excerpts showing the warmup retry loop
- verification scripts and checksum for our replays

What we did:
- Confirmed allocator contention triggered by duplicate warmup retries on the autoscaler sidecar.
- Deployed patch to stop duplicate warmup attempts and raised soft concurrency defaults for Canary pools.
- Verified the fallback routing exercised during the outage produced no data loss and maintained request ordering for completed responses.

What we will do next (concrete):
- 30-day config lock to stabilize concurrency and warmup behavior while we monitor (Automated rollout to Reserved clusters).
- Expand warmup observability (new metrics & alarms for retry storms).
- Complete a post-deployment soak test before removing the temporary soft-concurrency lift.

Credit proposal: pro-rated credit covering the incident window (8m) and a one-time SLA bridge for March. Details in the attached PDF.

Please find the packet here: https://drive.redwood/Shared/Atlas/DEAL-6742/evidence

Would you be available for the 30-min walkthrough on Mon 15 Mar 2027 10:00 PT? If not, suggest alternatives and we'll adjust.

Thanks again — we take this seriously and want to make sure your team has what you need for audits and internal RCA.

Best,

--
